title: Derived tensor and Tor under normalized coefficient encoding
statement: For a finite discrete commutative ring A, a scheme T, and any normalized Encoding e supplied by [lem-sf-finite-discrete-normalized-encoding], the actual termwise fixed-scalar derived equivalence admits a strong monoidal structure. For every internal derived object K and every ordered interval a <= b, its generic Tor-amplitude condition is equivalent both to HasProEtaleTorAmplitude for the ordinary section-module image and to generic Tor-amplitude for the fixed scalar image. These are the existing derived tensors and all degree-zero test modules, not a newly transferred tensor structure.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison] with $C=T_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}}$ and $R=p_T^*\underline A$; its site, sheafification and closed-monoidal hypotheses are exactly those used in step 2 and [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. It gives natural isomorphisms $E_R(M\otimes_RN)\cong E_RM\otimes_{R_{\mathrm{sec}}}E_RN$ and $E_R(R)\cong R_{\mathrm{sec}}$ for the coequalizer tensor of [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor] and the sheafified balanced tensor of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], given on local pure tensors by $m\otimes n\mapsto m\otimes n$ and compatible with associators, unitors and symmetry. By step 2, $E_T$ is $E_R$ followed by restriction of scalars along the ring-sheaf isomorphism $c_T:A_T\to R_{\mathrm{sec}}$. Under $c_T$ the balancing relations $m a\otimes n=m\otimes an$ over $R_{\mathrm{sec}}(U)$ and over $A_T(U)$ are the same relations, so the presheaf tensors of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] coincide sectionwise and hence after sheafification, with the same action through the first factor. Composing gives the natural, coherent comparison $E_T(M\otimes_{p_T^*\underline A}N)\cong E_TM\otimes_{A_T}E_TN$ with $E_T(p_T^*\underline A)\cong A_T$.

source.place: Tag 03EK, section-tensor-product (sheafified balanced tensor); comparison supplied by the cited internal/section tensor node

proof.text: Both equivalences preserve small coproducts: for a family $(M_i)$ and any $L$, the equivalence identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(E_T(\bigoplus_i M_i),L)$ with $\prod_i\operatorname{Hom}(E_TM_i,L)$, the coproduct universal property. By [lem-pe-internal-section-tensor-comparison], $E_R$ applied termwise identifies the direct-sum total tensor complexes, with differential $d(m\otimes n)=dm\otimes n+(-1)^{\deg m}m\otimes dn$, and preserves and reflects acyclicity and K-flat complexes in the acyclic-total-tensor sense of [def-pc-kflat-complex]; restricting scalars along $c_T$ as in step 5 changes none of this. The internal K-flatness of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] is [def-sfb-preserves-kflat-quasi-iso] ($P\otimes-$ and $-\otimes P$ preserve quasi-isomorphisms), which is the same test: the additive total tensor commutes with mapping cones, a map is a quasi-isomorphism exactly when its cone is acyclic, $0\to Q$ is a quasi-isomorphism exactly when $Q$ is acyclic, and the symmetry handles the second side. Hence an internal K-flat resolution $P\to K$ goes to an ordinary K-flat resolution $E_TP\to E_TK$. Computing [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom] and [def-weil-derived-tensor] on this same $P$ gives the natural comparison $D(E_T)(K\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{p_T^*\underline A}L)\cong D(E_T)K\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{A}D(E_T)L$.

source.place: K-flat computation of derived tensor, with the explicit acyclic-test argument; definitions in the cited tensor nodes

proof.text: Every ordinary module sheaf in degree zero is the image of an internal module sheaf in degree zero, and conversely. For each such test $N$, steps 2 and 6 identify $H^i(K\otimes^{\mathrm L}N)$ with its image under the exact equivalence. Since the equivalence reflects zero objects, the vanishing tests in [def-weil-proetale-tor-amplitude] are equivalent for every integer $i$ and every $N$. This proves preservation and reflection of each specified interval $[a,b]$, not merely existence of some finite interval.

lean.statement:
theorem encoding_tensor_tor [Finite A] [DiscreteTopology A]
    (T : Scheme.{u}) (e : Encoding A T) :
    Nonempty (e.fixedDerived.functor.Monoidal) ∧
    (∀ (K : DerivedCategory (Internal A T)) (a b : ℤ), a ≤ b →
      (DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn _ a b K ↔
        Scheme.HasProEtaleTorAmplitude T A (e.ordinaryDerived.functor.obj K) a b)) ∧
    (∀ (K : DerivedCategory (Internal A T)) (a b : ℤ), a ≤ b →
      (DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn _ a b K ↔ DerivedCategory.torAmplitudeIn _ a b
        (e.fixedDerived.functor.obj K)))
